recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No further FHIR-29803 source change is recommended; any future desire to restyle later Bundle.entry.fullUrl ElementDefinition wording should be handled under a separate fullUrl-focused tracker.
issue_request: FHIR-29803 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It requested conformance-language cleanup in the Bundle Resource URL & Uniqueness section: use SHALL for fullUrl and UUID requirements, replace confusing MAY-not wording with MAY omit fullURLs, use MAY for multiple versions, fix the information typo, and avoid confusion around fullUrl expectations for Bundle entries.
initial_application: Commit c7eb855076a1d5d1ed930925352094a96d7d0807 applied the requested Bundle notes edits, and follow-up commit a41e7958c85a2583535192048e11abfbfdf13be4 corrected the accidental 'SHALL must' phrase. No existing FHIR-29803 Issue-Reconcile-Key commit was present on the combined branch before this audit.
additional_context: Bundle is active in source/fhir.ini. Current source/bundle/bundle-notes.xml contains the SHALL/MAY wording and corrected spelling, while source/bundle/structuredefinition-Bundle.xml contains bdl-15 and Bundle.entry.fullUrl formal fullUrl requirements. Later related issues FHIR-27813 and FHIR-43106 refined the formal definition and exception wording; FHIR-43106 and adjacent FHIR-43101 are already represented on the combined branch. Confluence minutes confirm the FHIR-I vote and intent that entries MAY omit fullUrl; direct Zulip searches found no conflicting issue-specific discussion.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current authoritative Bundle narrative and formal fullUrl definitions already convey the FHIR-29803 decision, and adding fullUrl wording beside every Using Bundles resource sentence would be redundant with the adjacent Resource URL section and could create future maintenance drift.
